title: Stellar Evolution Stretch
welcome_lead: Combine HR diagrams, fusion stages and remnant types in exam-style questions.
meta_desc: GCSE Astronomy stretch: stellar evolution stages, remnants and exam-style reasoning.
final_note: You can connect a star's mass to its full life story.

concepts.def: Massive bloated star fusing heavier elements before supernova.
Shell of gas shed by a dying low-mass star.
Final fusion product in massive stars; cannot release energy.
Remnant of very massive star; gravity traps even light.
~1.4 solar masses; white dwarf maximum mass.
Fusion creating heavier elements in stellar cores.

walkthroughs.body_html: A star above ~8 solar masses fuses ever heavier elements up to iron. Iron fusion absorbs energy, so the core collapses, rebounds, and the star explodes as a supernova leaving a neutron star or black hole.
The Sun will exit the main sequence in ~5 billion years, become a red giant, shed a planetary nebula, and end as a white dwarf about Earth's size, cooling slowly for trillions of years.
State the mass range, give the path (main sequence -> giant phase -> remnant), and link to evidence (e.g., HR diagram position, supernova remnants like the Crab Nebula).

mcqs.q: What remnant forms after a very massive star's supernova if its core exceeds ~3 solar masses?
options: Black hole
White dwarf
Brown dwarf
Red giant

mcqs.q: Why does iron stop fusion in a massive star's core?
options: Iron fusion absorbs energy
Iron is too dense to compress
Iron repels itself electrically
Iron evaporates first

mcqs.q: What defines a star as being on the 'main sequence'?
options: It fuses hydrogen into helium in its core.
It is made of fire.
It is the largest stage of a star's life.
It is the hottest stage.

mcqs.q: Why is Jupiter classified as a gas giant?
options: It is the hottest stage.
Its bulk is mostly hydrogen and helium with no defined solid surface.
It is mostly air like Earth's atmosphere.
It is made of fire.

mcqs.q: Why don't we have a solar eclipse every new moon?
options: The Moon's orbit is tilted, so it usually passes above or below the Sun's apparent position.
Because clouds block them.
Eclipses happen randomly.
It is the hottest stage.
